title: Equal-capacity retarded-gravity search on fresh two-sided Halpha galaxy rotation curves
hypothesis: One causal finite-propagation response to the present baryonic growth proxy predicts fresh Halpha circular speeds at fixed optical radii better than instantaneous baryonic and flexible ordinary galaxy models, while its unchanged radial behavior and two-sided asymmetry survive held-out tests.

discovery_policy.universal_gravity_track: Require one unchanged causal propagation cell to improve the primary speed, both fixed radial replays, broad mass and activity halves, selection-aware nulls, and all applicable local and GW-speed gates.
discovery_policy.phenomenon_publication_track: Retain a reproducible propagation-timescale, activity, radius, or side-asymmetry relation that beats ordinary held-out controls on its actual domain even if it cannot be universal gravity.

theory.response_rule: At radius r, log(V)=log(V_instantaneous)+0.5*log(mu_R), with log(mu_R) proportional to the stellar specific-growth proxy times a nonnegative retarded path delay and a frozen radial window.
theory.static_limit: Every candidate returns mu_R=1 when the baryonic growth proxy is zero.
theory.causality: Every delay is nonnegative, propagation speed is positive and no greater than c, and no future or advanced support is admitted.
theory.local_limit: The same closure is evaluated at one AU with a conservative Solar fractional mass-change rate and must stay within the frozen local deviation bound.
theory.universal_speed_rule: A candidate is universal-track eligible only when its direct propagation speed satisfies the GW170817/GRB 170817A bound; slower cells remain testable only as effective local phenomena or failure-space representatives.

external_constraints.label: Carlip, Aberration and the Speed of Gravity
external_constraints.scope: In Lorentz-covariant gravity, velocity-dependent terms cancel naive aberration at leading order.

external_constraints.label: Yahalom, Retardation Effects in Gravitation
external_constraints.scope: Prior proposal that galactic retardation can alter rotation without dark matter.

external_constraints.label: Gomez-Lopez et al. HRS Halpha kinematic survey
external_constraints.scope: Independent photometric, Halpha-flux, and two-sided rotation-curve data source.

prior_equivalence: The single-path luminal niche is a known retarded-potential control, not a novel theory.
The near-zone compensated niche represents the known cancellation class of Lorentz-covariant weak-field theories.

A constant-speed subluminal response at one radius is amplitude-degenerate with a luminal response. The frozen finite-carrier niche is non-equivalent only through its size-dependent transition from c to a subluminal floor, and a floor that fails the GW-speed bound cannot be promoted as universal gravity merely because it fits galaxies.
A multi-path echo is potentially a distinct synthesis but requires an explicit carrier, scattering geometry, energy accounting, and lensing/GW tests before any theory claim.
Algebraic non-equivalence is not historical novelty; every positive survivor requires a dedicated prior-art audit.
claim_limits: Integrated Halpha luminosity is a recent star-formation proxy, not a measured past baryonic mass history.
Stellar mass plus optical size is not a complete baryonic mass map and omits direct atomic and molecular gas mass.
A fitted activity-delay correlation can be ordinary feedback, turbulence, morphology, or selection rather than retarded gravity.
The fixed-radius Halpha curve is an ionized-gas kinematic observable, not the speed of every star.
Item 27 will test fading gravitational memory separately; Item 26 admits finite causal paths but no free long-lived memory state.

observable_lineage.baryons: HRS stellar mass, i-band light, effective radius, optical radius, and HI-deficiency state frozen before response access.
observable_lineage.growth_proxy: Extinction-adjusted integrated Halpha luminosity converted to an SFR proxy and divided by frozen stellar mass.
observable_lineage.response: Approaching and receding Halpha rotation curves queried by exact exploration HRS identity only after sample and candidate freeze; velocities are interpolated independently at three fixed multiples of reff.

sample.rule: Exclude every predecessor name and coordinate before ranking. Divide the 80 predictor-quality survivors into four equal stellar-mass strata, seal four HMAC-ranked identities per stratum, and assign the remaining identities to five folds before querying any rotation curve.

candidate_generator.algorithm: numpy.random.Generator(PCG64) with four exactly balanced causal propagation niches before response-independent local, positivity, and causality filters
candidate_generator.synthetic_injection_rule: Exact admissible indices frozen before response access; one target-blind high-support non-equivalent injection per niche, with the finite-carrier injection required to have a subluminal floor.

evaluation.baseline_instantaneous_baryonic: training-only affine relation in the stellar baryonic velocity proxy sqrt(G Mstar/r)
evaluation.baseline_flexible_nuisance: fixed ridge regression on stellar mass, size, Halpha specific activity, ellipticity, inclination, HI deficiency, distance, optical concentration, environment, and predeclared interactions
evaluation.primary_loss: galaxy-balanced out-of-fold mean squared log10 speed at 1.3 reff
